name: RV-over-IV cheap-gamma breakout — realized outruns implied (1h)
rationale: ECONOMIC MECHANISM: the MIRROR of the VRP harvest and the second untested side of the IV-RV dislocation. When vol_realized crosses ABOVE dvol, realized is outrunning what options priced — the market is UNDER-hedged and a genuine directional move is already underway that dealers haven't caught up to. This is the 'options are cheap relative to what's actually happening' regime; realized-vol continuation is empirically stickier here (vol clustering: high RV follows high RV). We confirm with price momentum so we ride expansion WITH-trend, not into a knife. Entry: vol_realized clears a fitted floor AND dvol sits below a fitted ceiling (implied lagging realized -> options cheap) AND recent return is positive (the move is up). The other side is complacent vol sellers who wrote too-cheap options and are now short gamma into a real move, forced to buy spot to hedge -> their hedging FLOW is the fuel for the continuation. Economically OPPOSITE regime to VRP-harvest (same two features, inverted sign) -> must not be double-counted. Exit: vol_realized crosses down through a fitted level (the expansion is fading) or stop/TP/time. DISCONFIRMER 1: if an unconditional momentum long (drop the RV>IV cross) matches the deflated Sharpe, the dislocation trigger adds no timing edge and this is plain trend-following. DISCONFIRMER 2: IV-RV crossunders are symmetric to direction — if the price-momentum confirmation is doing all the work, the vol cross is noise. HARD CAVEAT: ~148 DVOL points -> paper-only.
catalyst: realized vol overtaking implied — under-hedged dealers chasing a live directional move
